## ELI5

Prevent two simultaneous saves from silently overwriting one another.

## What Changed

Route a new destination through the existing hardlink/exclusive-copy promotion helper. A competing save now receives a collision error while the earlier saved destination remains intact. The failed session retains its existing temporary-file cleanup; no recovery copy is promised. Explicit replacement retains its existing branch.

## Why

Two manual downloads can both observe an absent destination, then both rename onto it and report success. The later rename silently replaces the first saved file. This affects the desktop remote-file and artifact save flows.

src/main/ipc/filesystem/downloads/filesystem-download-handlers.ts fs:saveDownloadedFile and fs:finishDownloadedFile; src/renderer/src/runtime/files/reads/runtime-remote-file-download.ts:streamDownloadedFile.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #50578

N/A — this backend filesystem fix has no graphical layout change. The reproducible before/after behavior is recorded below.

Before/after data-level reproduction of the same input:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Two concurrent registered fs:finishDownloadedFile calls returned fulfilled/fulfilled and left only the later payload at the chosen destination. | Exactly one finish succeeds and the other reports a collision. The successful payload remains intact, both temporary files are gone, and neither session remains registered. |

No graphical layout change is included. The evidence above is from the production operation; no desktop screenshot is claimed.

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally through the production-entry reproduction described above
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below
- [x] Every added test fails without this change and avoids the test anti-patterns

With a local Electron IPC/dialog facade and real file handles/files, two start calls select the same absent destination, append different payloads, then finish concurrently. runtime.pr50624:
## ELI5

Keep a streamed download alive while its chunks are being saved, and clean it up after it becomes idle.

## What Changed

Refresh the existing cleanup timer only after a chunk has been written successfully. Reuse the native timer and retain the 30-minute cleanup interval, cancellation and renderer-lifetime cleanup.

## Why

The download session cleanup timer was armed once at start. Remote files and artifacts whose successful chunk writes continued longer than 30 minutes were deleted mid-transfer, even though the session was active.

Production callers:

- src/renderer/src/runtime/files/reads/runtime-remote-file-download.ts:streamDownloadedFile sequentially reads 384 KiB chunks and calls fs:appendDownloadedFileChunk
- src/main/ipc/filesystem/downloads/filesystem-download-handlers.ts:startDownloadedFile and appendDownloadedFileChunk

## Linked Issue

Fixes #50623

## Visual Proof

N/A — this change affects backend processing and has no graphical layout change. The production behavior is reproduced below.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The timer was measured from session creation, so at the scaled equivalent of 40 minutes the active session and its staging bytes had already been deleted. | Successful progress keeps the session and exact bytes available. The later idle interval removes them. A failed write does not extend the session lifetime. |

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested the source-level production reproduction described here
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below
- [x] No permanent tests added; the policy reason and baseline-failing manual reproduction are provided

No permanent IPC wiring or elapsed-time test was added, following the repository test policy. The linked issue contains the complete standalone probe. The original source fails the active-session assertion; the changed source passes active-progress, idle-cleanup and failed-write cases. Native timers and real file writes are used; only the long timeout is scaled and the Electron dialog/IPC boundary is supplied locally.

Use the standalone reproduction in the linked issue. From the source checkout:

```sh
ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1 node --import tsx /absolute/path/to/repro.mjs .
```

Locally exercised on Linux with Node 24.22.3. No macOS, Windows, graphical desktop, physical remote host or live external provider execution is claimed.

Final integrated validation: 32 focused regression tests in 22 files passed, including the unchanged archive-write failure case that had timed out under earlier heavy concurrent checking. The Drive performance contract passed separately (1 file/1 test). Changed-code quality passed with zero new findings across 129 changed paths; final touched-file formatting and git diff --check passed. Node typechecking passed for 17,026 files and web typechecking for 16,094 files using the repository-supported Bun compiler with one worker. These are aggregate validation results for the prepared contributions, not per-PR test counts.

The required `pnpm check:changed --base=9890ea181c0f9ae59fb82da64c4a6fbc0504a817` was attempted after the final edits. Its workspace-package build is blocked because this environment rejects the tsx CLI local IPC socket (`listen EPERM`). The default tsrs typechecker was also terminated with SIGKILL; the supported Bun typechecking route completed successfully. The complete gate/build is not claimed to pass and still requires CI.

## Performance

One native Timeout.refresh call per successfully written chunk, reusing the existing timer. The renderer streams sequential 384 KiB chunks, so this adds no timer allocation, background polling or extra file operation.

## Risk

**Level:** Low

Active sessions can now last longer than 30 minutes in total, which is the intended behavior. Abandoned sessions still expire after 30 idle minutes. Failed writes do not refresh the timer; cancellation and renderer destruction still close the session. The elapsed-time probe used a scaled native timeout, not a 40-minute wall-clock run.

A plain revert restores the previous behavior; no schema migration is introduced.
